Week 3 course content: Java conditional statements: if, if-else, nested if and switch
ILOs:
- Develop and test Java programs that use if-else and switch statements to make decisions.
Contact units stated by the syllabus: lecture 2, laboratory 1
records.target: - Individual timed coding test in which students write if-else programs from memory.

before.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
before.sourceQuote: Develop and test Java programs that use if-else and switch statements to make decisions
before.targetQuote: Individual timed coding test in which students write if-else programs from memory
before.explanation: The activity does have students write if-else programs, so it practises the action verb and subject, but it stops at Apply: the ILO asks learners to develop AND test programs, and a timed test from memory gives no opportunity to run and test the program or to use switch. It also offers a single format with no alternative route for learners who cannot code under time pressure, and no reference material or worked examples to support recall of syntax. The gap is the missing testing step and the missing switch practice, plus the single-format support.
before.draft: - Individual coding exercise in which students write if-else and switch programs from worked examples and syntax notes, then run and test each program against several inputs and correct any faulty logic; students who prefer not to work under time pressure may complete the same exercise untimed with the notes available.

after.targetQuote: Individual timed coding test in which students write if-else programs from memory
